title: Responsive Images
definition: Using the `sizes` attribute or the `fill` prop to handle images whose physical size on the screen changes across different breakpoints (mobile vs desktop).
simpleExplanation: If you hardcode `width={500}`, the image is always 500px wide. But what if you want an image that stretches to fill the entire width of the user's screen? You use the `fill` property, and you tell Next.js the `sizes` so it knows exactly what file sizes to generate.
realWorldExample: A Hero Banner at the top of a webpage. It needs to be 400px wide on a phone, and 2000px wide on a 4K monitor. The `fill` prop combined with CSS `object-cover` makes this effortless.

basic: If you use the `fill` property on an `<Image>`, do you still need to provide `width` and `height` properties?
intermediate: If you use `fill`, what CSS position class MUST be applied to the parent `<div>` wrapping the image?

answers.question: Need width/height?
answers.answer: No! `fill` replaces the need for width and height. It tells the image to automatically stretch to match the exact dimensions of its parent container.

answers.question: CSS on parent?
answers.answer: `position: relative` (or `absolute`/`fixed`). If the parent is not relative, the filled image will escape the container and literally fill the entire browser window.
